cases.description: A schema whose check of the spine counts more than 1,000,000 pairs is schema-invalid, too complex to check (§9.3, decision AA1). An allOf of 1,010 branches giving one typed reference at member a and 1,010 giving another at member b counts (1,010 + 2)² = 1,024,144 pairs of schema objects that apply together at the root and whose declarations below could disagree: the branches and $defs/a against the branches and $defs/b, and the root with every one of them and with itself. Without the bound the schema is valid, as its near miss shows. The count and the bound are an agent's reading recorded in decision AA1.

The near miss of spine-work-over-bound: the same schema with 990 branches in each group counts (990 + 2)² = 984,064 pairs, within the bound of 1,000,000, so it can be used, and the record is valid (§9.3, decision AA1).
A member that x-vmd-list does not define, sorted, may come from a newer minor version, so the schema is feature-unsupported, not schema-invalid (§9.1, §9.3, decision AA2).
A value of x-vmd-list's type that this version does not define, set, is feature-unsupported (§9.3, decision AA2).
A member that x-vmd-ref does not define, order, is feature-unsupported (§9.3, decision AA2).
A value of x-vmd-ref's cardinality that this version does not define, some, is feature-unsupported (§9.3, decision AA2).
The near miss of the unknown members and values: every member of x-vmd-list and x-vmd-ref, with values this version defines, can be used (§9.3).

A member that x-vmd-list defines, keys, with a value of the wrong form, a string where a list stands, is schema-invalid, not feature-unsupported (§9.3). That a wrong form is not an unknown value is an agent's reading recorded in decision AA2.
A $dynamicRef is allowed (§9.2, decision AA3): this recursive schema can be used, and the kid whose name is a number is a schema violation, which the validator reaches through the $dynamicRef.

Every $dynamicAnchor that a $dynamicRef may land on counts as off the spine, so an x-vmd-list reached only through it is schema-invalid (§9.2, §9.3, decision AA3). dynamic-ref-tree is the near miss: a $dynamicRef that reaches no declaration.

A schema with several problems gets one code: an unknown x-vmd-* keyword beside $id, which alone is schema-invalid (validation/configuration/schema-with-id), makes it feature-unsupported, since a newer version may explain the rest (§9.1, decision AA4, item 1).
An x-vmd-ref on a schema without type, which allows a string, needs format: uri-reference, so x-vmd-ref alone is schema-invalid (§9.3, decisions U18 and AA4, item 2).
The near miss of ref-without-type: a schema for a $ref object writes type: object, which allows no string, and can be used (§9.3, decision AA4, item 2).
A schema file holds an object, so a file holding the boolean schema true, which 2020-12 allows, is schema-invalid (§9.2, decision AA4, item 3).

Two patterns that apply together and bring unequal declarations to a name that a properties lists, rx, are schema-invalid at load, although rx is listed one level down and only a record with a root member rx would bring them together, which is conservative (§9.3, decision AA4, item 4).

The near miss of patterns-meet-at-listed-name: no name that a properties lists matches both patterns, so only a member name in the data, such as rx, could bring them together, and the check waits for the record. The schema can be used, and a record without such a member is valid (§9.3, decision AA4, item 4).

Two additionalProperties of an allOf with unequal declarations meet only at a member that the data names, so the schema can be used, and a record without members is valid (§9.3, decision AA4, item 4).

An array's items and its x-vmd-list's additional bring unequal declarations to an item only when the item's key is one the list's items does not name, which the data decides, so the schema can be used (§9.3, decision AA4, item 4).
An identifier with a string value inside data, here $anchor inside a const, is schema-invalid, which narrows 2020-12 (§9.2, decision AA4, item 5).
The near miss of identifier-in-data: an $anchor member whose value is not a string is data, compared as written, so the schema can be used (§9.2, decision AA4, item 5).

A declaration that the spine reaches, at a, and that a oneOf branch reaches too, at b, is schema-invalid, so that it never applies at one place and silently not at the other (§9.3, decision AA4, item 6).
The near miss of declaration-on-and-off-spine: a declaration that the spine reaches at two places can be used (§9.3).
An additionalProperties of a section also takes its $sections, so a keyed list there is checked as $sections, whose keys can only be @key, and is schema-invalid (§9.3, decision AA4, item 7).
The near miss of sections-through-additional-properties: properties: {$sections: false} keeps $sections out of the additionalProperties, and the schema can be used (§9.3, decision AA4, item 7).
